title: Files and where programming is heading
subtitle: Variables vanish when the program ends; files remember. Then a glance at how programming grew up.

why.title: Why files
why.body: Variables live in RAM and disappear at exit. A file stores data on disk as a stream of bytes. Text files hold characters (readable, line-oriented); binary files hold raw bytes (compact, fast, not human-readable).

life.title: The file lifecycle
life.body: FILE *f = fopen("data.txt", "r"); returns a pointer, or NULL if opening fails — always check. Modes: r read, w write (truncates!), a append, r+ read/write; add b for binary. Then use fprintf/fscanf (formatted), fgets/fputs (lines), fread/fwrite (blocks), and finally fclose(f) so buffered data is flushed.

read.title: Reading until the end
read.body: Read in a loop until the function reports end of file: while (fscanf(f, "%d", &x) == 1) stops when a value could not be read. Checking feof before reading causes the classic “last line processed twice” bug.
read.steps: A file holds 5 numbers: 4 6 8 2 10. Read and sum. 4 + 6 + 8 + 2 + 10.

seek.title: Random access
seek.body: fseek(f, offset, SEEK_SET) moves the position; ftell reports it. With fixed-size records, record n starts at byte n × size, so any record can be read without scanning the rest.

paradigm.title: Paradigms
paradigm.body: Procedural (C): a program is functions acting on data. Object-oriented (C++, Java, Python): data and the functions that act on it are bundled in classes. Functional: programs are compositions of pure functions. Modern languages mix them.

trend.title: Recent trends
trend.body: Memory-safe languages (Rust), scripting for data and AI (Python), web and mobile (JavaScript/Kotlin), WebAssembly, AI coding assistants, open-source libraries and version control as everyday tools. C remains the language of operating systems, embedded devices and compilers — learning it teaches how the machine really works.
